title: Physics Lab runtime transition mutation fence
objective: Close the source-only runtime lifecycle reentrancy defect found by capacity mining: transition adapters must not be able to partially dismantle or recursively mutate PhysicsLabRuntime authority while an F2/F0 fidelity transaction is in flight.
acceptance: dispose or recursive runtime mutation from capture/transition callbacks rejects before any registry or fidelity population change
callback rejection leaves the runtime active, fully registered, authority-synchronized, and retryable
runtime transition guard always clears after callback failure
existing F2/F0 transition, capture ownership, deterministic ordering, and idempotent normal teardown remain unchanged
pure regressions prove no partial teardown or count drift; no Roblox Studio/engine evidence claim
notes: Independent exact-head audit of PR #366 at f50067d4dedbe548fc80aed2289b846644dd941c returned REQUEST_CHANGES despite green canonical CI 31482367736 and green Swarm engine-tests. The callback-local transition fence, hidden runtime facade, retry semantics, and generation-2 weak-key typing repair are sound, but current-main FidelityManager still dereferences caller-owned PolicyInputs before PhysicsLabRuntime raises transitionInFlight. A metatable-backed PolicyInputs __index can therefore call runtime.dispose while the guard is false and tear down both authority populations before the outer step fails. Repair by putting PR #335/equivalent no-execute PolicyInputs + hostile-time preflight in ancestry, or by extending the runtime mutation transaction/preflight over the full FidelityManager.step call window; add a regression proving policy-input evaluation cannot mutate runtime authority. The eventual integration head must also synthesize overlapping canonical recipe-fence PR #310 and rerun exact-head canonical CI plus live pr-ownership.
